newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani stocks end up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani stocks end up on short-covering.

text.p: Pakistani stocks ended up on short-covering on Wednesday despite three bomb explosions that killed a man and wounded three others in Karachi, and are likely to open mixed on Thursday, dealers said.
The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) 100-share index closed 17.75 points, or 1.30 percent, up at 1,379.26 amid 125 gainers and 115 losers. Turnover rose to 31 million shares from Tuesday's 27 million.
The main reason for the rise despite the bomb attacks was "the bullishness in Tuesday's kerb market after the official trading", one dealer said.
The index posted fresh gains because of a sharp rise in speculative stocks weighing heavily on the index, one broker said.
HUBCO rose 1.50 rupees to 32.25, PTCL 0.70 to 34.40, Dewan Salman Fibre 0.40 to 23.40 and Pakistan State Oil 4.00 to 328.
